bullets.text: Fourteen people have been killed in a strike on a monastery in Myanmar, with a rescue worker reporting the site was hit twice while civilians were gathered for a meditation retreat.
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the deadliest in the country's history, with at least 2,325 deaths reported, and is on track to be the largest outbreak ever.

More than 100 people have died after an artisanal goldmine collapsed due to a landslide in the Central African Republic, with local officials anticipating the death toll will rise as recovery efforts continue.

Traditional owners in Queensland are relieved that a proposed mining project on Pilungah Reserve, which was believed to hold critical minerals, will not proceed, avoiding a potential repeat of the Juukan Gorge disaster.

A new scheme to replace the NDIS for children with autism, called the Thriving Kids program, is facing questions from the Queensland Premier and many parents, as the state has refused to sign up for it.
A three-part documentary series is set to mark 25 years since the Tampa diplomatic stand-off, aiming to provide a nuanced perspective on the event that redefined Australia's border protection policy.
The upcoming Jackson Hole Symposium will focus on Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Marsh's first annual address, with market participants closely watching for insights into monetary policy.
Companies seeking to finance data center projects are increasingly issuing investment-grade debt to junk bond buyers, attracted by the higher yields.
Early labor-market data suggests that Artificial Intelligence's primary impact is currently more evident in wages than in overall employment levels.
